A sexist joke made about two attorneys during this case was dubbed the “worst joke in legal history.” For 10 points each:
[M] Name this court case, which resulted in the creation of the Hyde Amendment. Griswold v. Connecticut served as a major precedent for this court case.
[E] Roe v. Wade used the “right to privacy” principle to protect a women’s right to this practice. This practice is supported by the pro-choice movement.
column6: ANSWER: Abortion [or terminating a pregnancy; or ending a pregnancy]

column5: [H] This conservative Chief Justice appointed by Richard Nixon presided over Roe v. Wade. This Chief Justice would later abandon Roe in Thornburgh v. American College.
column6: ANSWER: Warren E. Burger [or Warren Earl Burger]

column5: One instrument from this country imitates the neighing and galloping of a horse in the piece Sai Ma. For 10 points each:
[H] Name this country. Traditional instruments from this country include the erhu and pipa.
column6: ANSWER: People’s Republic of China [or Zhōngguó or Zhōnghuá Rénmín Gònghéguó or PRC; do NOT accept or prompt on “Republic of China” or “Zhōnghuá Mínguó”]

column5: [M] Traditional Chinese instruments like the erhu and pipa are members of this instrument family. Members of this family in the orchestra include the cello and violin.
[E] The erhu and pipa are common fixtures in an opera style named after this city. An egg-shaped opera house called the National Centre for the Performing Arts is located in this capital of China.
column6: ANSWER: Beijing [or Peking; or Beiping; or Cambaluc; or Chung-tu; or Khan-baliq; or Pei Chih-li; or Pei-p’ing; or Ta-tu; or Yanjing; or Yen-ching; or Zhongdu]

column5: Bob Woodward secretly met in an underground parking garage in Rosslyn, Virginia with this man, whose family acknowledged his identity in 2005. For ten points each,

Identify this former deputy Director of the FBI, whose leaks helped Woodward and his partner at the Washington Post, Carl Bernstein, uncover a Presidential conspiracy. His real name and his nickname are both acceptable.
column6: W. Mark Felt (accept Deep Throat; accept William Mark Felt, Senior)

column5: Deep Throat helped Woodward and Bernstein untangle this scandal, which stemmed from a burglary at a Washington, D.C. office complex.
The Watergate scandal forced this US President to resign in 1974. His successor, Gerald Ford, controversially pardoned him a month later.
The Wikipedia article for this substance compares its viscosity to ketchup, but geologists probably haven’t tested that by pouring it out of a glass bottle. For ten points each,
Give this term for molten rock that has emerged onto or above the surface of the crust.
Among the types of lava are pahoehoe [pa-ho-ay-ho-ay], whose surface is billowing and smooth, and this type, with a craggly surface of “clinkers”. This name also has a Hawaiian derivation.
Lava that cools very rapidly without growing crystals may form this rock, often described as volcanic glass because it can break apart into sheets with sharp edges.
The highest mountain in Western Europe, Mont Blanc, is in the western part of this range. For ten points each,
Name this European mountain range. Mont Blanc lies on the border between Italy and France, before this range stretches to Switzerland.
This major European river has its source in the Swiss Alps; it then flows north, creates much of the border between France and Germany, and empties into the North Sea in the Netherlands.
This iconic, pyramid-shaped Alpine peak lies on the border between Switzerland and Italy. Hundreds of climbers have died on this peak, including four members of the first team to summit it in 1911.

The superstitious composer Gustav Mahler steadfastly refused to give his Song of the Earth its rightful status as a numbered symphony because, having seen what happened to men like Anton Bruckner and Franz Schubert, he was afraid of this number. For ten points each,
Name this number, the subject of a supposed “curse” on the composers of symphonies.
column6: nine (accept ninth; accept additional information like ninth symphony)

column5: The “curse of the ninth” is said to have started with this German composer, who was totally deaf when he conducted the premier of his Choral ninth symphony.

Before he succumbed to the curse of the ninth, Beethoven gave a massive concert in December 1808 where he premiered his Pastoral Symphony and this piece. This symphony doesn’t have a nickname, but it does feature Beethoven’s famous “short-short-short-long” motif.
column6: Fifth Symphony (accept Symphony Number 5 in C minor)

column5: The animals in class Chordata [kor-DAH-tuh] are mostly grouped into the tunicates and these animals. For ten points each,
Name this subphylum whose animals, including fish, mammals, and birds, all have backbones.
Almost all vertebrates are members of Gnathostomata [NATH-oh-sto-MAH-ta] because they have this body part, but some fish - such as hagfish, lampreys, and many long-extinct fish - don’t have one.
Most - but not all! - fish lack these body parts, instead using gills to filter oxygen out of water. Pneumonia is a condition affecting the alveoli in this organ.
Answer the following about murderous short stories by Edgar Allan Poe, for ten points each.
In one Poe short story, Montresor bricks Fortunato into a cellar wall after luring him in by promising him a “Cask of” this title wine.

This short story’s narrator plots to kill his housemate to rid himself of the man’s vulture-like eye, only to give himself away by tearing up his floorboards to reveal his dismembered victim to the police.
In this short story, Prospero tries desperately to avoid death, but is nonetheless killed in front of an ebony clock by a supernatural embodiment of this story’s title sickness.
column6: The Masque of the Red Death

column5: This empire’s religion worshipped the creator god Viracocha and revered its legendary founder, Manco Capac. For ten points each,
Name this pre-Columbian empire in South America, where Manco Capac was credited with founding the capital city of Cuzco.
In some stories, Manco Capac was the son of Inti, the Incan sun god, who was worshipped in this Incan city high in the Andes Mountains in modern Peru.
As the son of Inti, Manco Capac is said to have arisen from this major lake in the Andes, shared by modern Peru and Bolivia.
A nineteenth-century poem about this ancient author describes the emotions felt “On first looking into” this man’s works, as translated by George Chapman. For ten points each,
Name this Greek poet, whose attributed works include an epic poem about the Trojan War, the Iliad.
“On First Looking into Chapman’s Homer” is by a poet who also wrote an “Ode on a Grecian” object of this type. In the poem, this object is held up as the proof that “beauty is truth, truth beauty.”
column6: urn (accept Ode on a Grecian Urn)

column5: “On First Looking into Chapman’s Homer” and “Ode on a Grecian Urn” are poems by this English Romantic poet who had a rivalry with Lord Byron.
A player in this game, “KleinTsuboi,” became known as “Let Me Solo Her” for joining games to fight Malenia, Blade of Miquella for other players while wearing a pot on his head. For ten points each,
Name this 2022 open-world R.P.G. FromSoftware game distributed by Bandai Namco.

To commemorate his popularity among Elden Ring fans, Bandai sent Klein one of these bladed weapons inscribed with “Rise,Tarnished.” Klein fights Malenia with two katanas, which are a type of this weapon.
The worldbuilding behind Malenia and other characters in Elden Ring was done with the help of this American author of A Song of Ice and Fire.
column6: George R.R. Martin (accept George Raymond Richard Martin; prompt on “GRRM”)

column5: The 643 Edict of Rothari forbids killing those believed to be this type of person, because “Christian minds” should not believe that this type of person exists. For ten points each,
Name this type of supernatural person. Medieval “hunts” for these people were often just excuses to harass and kill unpopular women.
column6: witches (accept witchcraft and similar elaborations; accept sorcerers or sorceresses; accept warlocks)

column5: German Heinrich Kramer wrote this 15th century text, which argues that witchcraft is a heresy that needs to be punished via burning at the stake. This book’s Latin name indicates that this work’s knowledge is a weapon that can be used to fight witches.
column6: Malleus Maleficarum (accept The Witch Hammer; accept The Hammer of Witches)

column5: Malleus Maleficarum heavily cites this Scholastic thinker, a 13th century saint of the Catholic Church. This author’s Summa Theologica is a massive guide to Catholic theology.
This novel’s title character reads too many romantic novels, convinces himself that he’s a knight, and rides around on his elderly horse, Rocinante, getting into trouble. For ten points each,
Name this Spanish novel by Miguel de Cervantes [ser-VON-tays] about a man who attacks windmills because he imagines they’re giants.
column6: Don Quijote [kee-HOH-tay] (accept The Ingenious Gentleman Don Quijote of La Mancha; accept El Ingenioso hidalgo Don Quixote de la Mancha)

column5: Don Quijote [don kee-HOH-tay] is accompanied on his misguided adventures by this man, his long-suffering servant.
While traveling with Don Quijote, Sancho Panza rides Dapple, a gray-brown one of these long-eared, horse-like animals.
This god is the father of Kartikeya and Ganesha, whose head he cut off in order to reach Parvati. For ten points each,
Name this destroyer god often depicted with a blue throat he got from drinking the halahala poison.
Shiva is revered in Shaivism, a major denomination of this Indian religion.
With Brahma and Vishnu, Shiva forms this group of three gods in Hinduism.
According to folklore, this event was “signalled” by the coded announcement “this meeting can do nothing further to save the country.” For ten points each,
Name this 1773 riot in which protestors boarded the Eleanor, the Dartmouth, and the Beaver and dumped their cargo into a harbor.
This patriot and cousin of a future President gave the supposedly coded message at the meeting that preceded the Tea Party.

The British responded to the Boston Tea Party by closing the Port of Boston and revoking the charter of Massachusetts, each of which was part of this set of acts. These acts sought to punish all Bostonians, not just the perpetrators.
Dutch painter Piet Mondrian [PEET MON-dree-yon] created Broadway Boogie-Woogie with these colors among thick black lines and white squares. For ten points each,
Give the term that refers to the pigments red, yellow, and blue.
Mondrian’s late works, like Broadway Boogie-Woogie, are the geometric form of this type of work, contrasted with realistic art. Mondrian represented ideas instead of images of reality.
column6: abstract art (accept word forms like abstraction; accept geometric abstract art)

column5: In the 1960s, Mondrian’s work was adapted by Yves Saint Laurent [EEV sawn lah-RAWN] into this art form. The adaptation transformed Mondrian’s geometric designs into A-line works in this art form.
column6: fashion (accept clothes; accept descriptions like wearable art; accept dresses)

column5: This man suffered from indigestion, lust-driven insomnia, and a general distaste for how downright informal Americans were during this 1909 trip to the United States. For ten points each,
Name this Austrian thinker whose theories of psychoanalysis became decidedly more popular in the US than in Europe.

Freud was one of several thinkers invited by Clark University to speak in America; another was this colleague, who coined the theory of the “collective unconscious” and recommended that Freud cheat on his wife in order to get some sound sleep. Freud declined.

Freud’s lectures in America were largely based on his 1899 work on The Interpretation of these unconscious events, which mainly occur during REM sleep. Freud complained of having awful examples of these events during his American trip.
column6: dreams (accept The Interpretation of Dreams; accept Die Traumdeutung)

column5: These substances are classified as “strong” or “weak” based on whether it completely dissociates into its ions, not - as commonly misunderstood by beginning chemistry students - on how good it is at reacting with bases. For ten points each,
Give this term for solutions with a pH value less than 7.
The concentration of an unknown acid can be judged by this lab technique, in which drops of a known base are slowly added to the solution. An indicator is then used to determine changes in pH.
This strong acid is commonly used in high school titration labwork because it is relatively safe to handle. The extremely low pH of gastric juices is due to this acid.
column6: hydrochloric acid (accept HCl; prompt on “stomach acid”)

column5: Give the following about the traditional order of operations in arithmetic, for ten points each.

Multiplication comes before addition in the order of operations because multiplication is repeated addition; similarly, this operation of repeated multiplication comes before multiplication and division.
column6: exponentiation (accept word forms like exponents; accept “raising to a power”; prompt on “squaring”, “cubing”, or other specific examples of an exponent)

column5: These symbols are used to escape the normal order of operations; that is, “3 plus 4 minus 5” will be different if these symbols are placed around the “4 minus 5”.
column6: parentheses (or parenthesis; accept brackets; accept braces)

column5: With that said - addition has this property, so “3 plus 4 plus 5” gives the same result even if you do put parentheses around two of the numbers. Multiplication also has this property, but subtraction does not.
column6: associative property (accept word forms, like associate)

column5: American author Ambrose Bierce frequently wrote about this conflict, during which he fought in the 9th Indiana Infantry. For ten points each,
Name this war. In Bierce’s short story “Chickamauga,” a small deaf boy unknowingly sleeps through an 1863 battle that was one of this war’s bloodiest.

Bierce also wrote “What I Saw of” this 1862 battle of the Civil War, during which he actually fought. The short story gives a soldier’s view of Grant’s victory at this Tennessee battle, which was also called Pittsburg Landing.
column6: Shiloh (accept Battle of Shiloh; accept What I Saw of Shiloh)

column5: In a short story titled “An Occurrence at” this place, Confederate civilian Payton Farquhar [FAR-kwar], who is executed by the Union for trying to sabotage the title structure.
column6: Owl Creek Bridge (accept An Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge; do not accept or prompt on partial answers or on answers that are out of order)

column5: Give the following about the myriad ways that western colonization of Australia ruined things, for ten points each.
Most obviously, colonizers sought to assimilate or remove these indigenous people of mainland Australia.

In 1859, Thomas Austin released 24 of these animals into Australia, assuming they could do little harm; they had no predators and bred very quickly. Within 50 years, Western Australia started building a 2,000-mile-long fence meant to keep these creatures out.
In 1932, Western Australia deployed machine gunners to deal with these flightless birds. The attempts didn’t really prevent farm losses, so Australia infamously lost the “War” against these birds.
This type of wave is audible if its frequency is between 20 and 20,000 Hertz. For ten points each,
Name this phenomenon whose vibrations travel through room temperature air at roughly 3443 meters per second.
The intensity of a sound wave is measured in this logarithmic unit, which also has several applications in electronics. A jet engine’s noise commonly registers 140 of these units.
column6: decibel (accept dB; accept bel or B)

column5: While moving through air, sound waves are classified as this type of wave, because the medium moves perpendicular to the motion of the wave. In the main alternative, a transverse wave, the medium moves in parallel.
Heats of reaction are often provided in this unit of energy, rather than kilojoules, because they are convenient to measure in calorimeters. For ten points each,
Name this imperial unit of heat energy that’s about 4.18 Joules. Most often, it’s used to measure the energy content of foods.
column6: calories (accept cal; accept kilocalories or kcal)

column5: Heats of reactions are convenient to write using calories because calorimeters are often filled with water, and in imperial units, this quantity for water is exactly 1 calorie per gram degree Celsius.
If the heat of reaction is measured in one of these devices of fixed volume, you’ll probably see it reported in Joules. These calorimeters have intrinsic heat capacities reported by the manufacturer.

In 1996, Billy Bailey became the most recent, and possibly last, person to suffer this fate, which is only legal in Delaware, New Hampshire, and Washington, and only then as a backup method. For ten points each,
Name this punishment. It was once commonly performed via the long drop, but it has largely been replaced by more “humane” methods.
Four of this man’s conspirators - including Mary Surratt and George Atzerodt - were hanged at the Washington Arsenal on July 7, 1865. This man was, instead, shot in a burning barn on April 26th.

After the 1862 US-Dakota War, on President Lincoln’s orders, 38 Dakota men were hanged in this state’s town of Mankato, the largest mass execution in American history. A year later, the Dakota were exiled from this state.
This river flows east-to-west into the Atlantic Ocean and lends its name to two African countries on its banks. For ten points each,
Name this second longest river in Africa.
The Congo River separates two national capitals: Brazzaville and this megacity. This capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is the largest city in Africa by size.

The Congo River basin is home to both species of the genus Pan: chimpanzees and this smaller relative, whose habitat is south of the river. Scientists speculate that, because these primates can’t swim well, the formation of the Congo River may have caused the speciation between chimpanzees and these primates.
In calculus, a line is known by this name if it just barely intersects a curve at one point, as contrasted with a secant line, which cuts through the curve at two nearby points. For ten points each,
Give this mathematical term. In trigonometry, this word names a function that is equal to the sine function divided by the cosine function.

Finding a tangent line provides a way to calculate this value for a curved line at a given point. For a straight line, finding this value is much simpler; it’s always the same, and it is equal to the line’s rise over run.

This French mathematician’s work on finding tangent lines helped lay the foundation for calculus, but he’s better known today for inventing the rectangular coordinate system. Please give the name of the man, not the coordinate system.
A poem by this man opens with the advice “Go home and write / a page tonight. And let that page come out of you- Then, it will be true.” For ten points each,
Name this co-leader of an early 20th century cultural movement in New York, a Black American jazz poet who wrote “Theme for English B” and the collection The Weary Blues.
column6: Langston Hughes (accept James Mercer Langston Hughes)

column5: Hughes was a dominant figure in the “Renaissance” of this Manhattan neighborhood, which was predominantly Black in the early 20th century. A short Hughes poem named for this place opens by asking “What happens to a dream deferred?”

This Hughes poem from The Weary Blues notes “I am the darker brother. They send me to eat in the kitchen / When company comes.” This poem is a direct response to Walt Whitman’s “I Hear America Singing,” and its title is the first two words of the poem.
Tref is, essentially, the opposite of this adjective, which is equivalent to halal in Islam. For ten points each,
Name this Hebrew adjective that describes foods that observant Jews will eat.

Invertebrates are generally not kosher, except for these insects, which conveniently abound in the Bible. These insects terrorize the Egyptians in the eighth plague in Exodus and are consumed by John the Baptist in the wilderness.
Observant Jews also refuse to eat this meat, according to a prohibition against eating animals that chew their own cud. This meat is foresworn by Muslims as well.
column6: pork (accept pig meat; prompt on “bacon”, “sausage”, or other foods that could be made from pork or other sources)

column5: On one particularly deadly day during this decades-long conflict, Lord Mountbatten was assassinated by a bomb planted on his boat and a convoy was ambushed at Warrenpoint. For ten points each,
Name this period of off-and-on sectarian violence and rioting that was largely ended by the 1998 Good Friday Agreement.
The Troubles took place in cities like Derry, Belfast, and Dublin on this island, whose Northern region remains part of the United Kingdom.

In April 1916, a massive rebellion swept through Ireland and was brutally suppressed, with most of its leaders being executed. The rebellion began on the day after this major religious holiday, and thus became known as this holiday’s “Rising.”

This man reproduced a still image from 1953’s Niagara for his Marilyn Diptych silkscreen, which features 25 hypercolored copies and 25 smudged black and white copies of Marilyn Monroe’s face. For ten points each,
Name this Pop artist.
Warhol’s most famous silkscreens are likely his depictions of these common grocery items, produced by Campbell’s.

In addition to his paintings and silkscreens, Warhol created over 100 of these artworks, including a five-hour-long one titled Sleep that depicts John Giorno sleeping and an eight-hour-long one that depicts a slow-motion view of the Empire State Building.
column6: films (accept movies; accept anti-films or anti-movies)

column5: Sinkholes are common when groundwater is able to circulate and the underlying ground is made of this rock. For ten points each,
Name this rock that is made up of various forms of calcium carbonate, such as calcite. Metamorphosis of this rock can create marble.
The dissolution of limestone can create these empty underground spaces, where stalactites and stalagmites from from dripping mineral water.
Caves, sinkholes, and underground rivers are commonly found in this type of limestone-rich landscape with a German name.
column6: Karst (accept additional information, like karst landscape, karst topography, etc.)

column5: The first page of a novel by this author is a bonafide checklist for common tropes in the rest of his writing: a male protagonist is alone in his apartment, cooking pasta and listening to classical music, when he is disturbed by a phone call from a mysterious woman. For ten points each,
Name this modern Japanese author of The Wind-up Bird Chronicle.

Toru Okada, the protagonist of The Wind-up Bird Chronicle, is tasked with finding one of these missing pets, who also appear in almost all of Murakami’s works. Okada eventually finds the pet waiting at home, meowing as though Okada were the missing one.

Okada de-stresses by ironing these items of clothing, for which he has a 12-step process that cannot be done out of order. In The Great Gatsby, Daisy becomes hysterical at the sight of a closet full of these items in Gatsby’s house.
This man wrote five essays under the name of “Helvidius,” arguing against Alexander Hamilton’s “Pacificus” in essays regarding American neutrality. For ten points each,
Name this American founding father who served as Thomas Jefferson’s Secretary of State and, later, as the fourth US President.
Madison is known as the “Father of” this foundational American document, having drafted much of the theory behind its seven articles.

Before quarreling with Hamilton, Madison and Hamilton joined with John Jay to write the pro-Constitution Federalist Papers. The essays were published under this joint pseudonym, meant to evoke a Roman sense of friendliness toward the people.
Christian texts have provided lyrics for many pieces of European music. Answer the following about Christian choral music, for ten points each.
The King James Bible inspired Handel’s Messiah oratorio, which includes this chorus that celebrates the “King of Kings and Lord of Lords.”

This Catholic prayer begins “Ellen’s Third Song,” a work by Franz Schubert in which the singer pleads to the title religious figure to “hear a maiden’s prayer.” This prayer’s full version is addressed to the “Mother of God.”

Sung texts like the “Credo” [kray-doh] and the “Kyrie” [kee-ree-ay] are among the sections of these pieces of Catholic liturgical music. Mozart left a Requiem one of these pieces unfinished at his death.
The AvengerCon scene of this show’s first episode reveals that, in the world of the MCU, Groot is only known to the general population as “Mr Tree.” For ten points each,
After wearing a golden bangle, Kamala Khan becomes the title superhero of this show, whose six episodes premiered in summer 2022.
Kamala Khan is played by this Pakistani-Canadian actress. The show is her first acting credit, and she will reprise the role in an upcoming MCU film.
Ms. Marvel premiered on this streaming service, which owns the rights to the MCU, as well as Star Wars.
Women languishing with mysterious or false illnesses appear frequently in fiction. For ten points each,
In an Edgar Allan Poe short story about the “Fall of” this family, Madeline becomes sick and seems to die, only to claw her way out of her tomb to actually die alongside her brother, Roderick.
column6: Usher (accept House of Usher; accept The Fall of the House of Usher)

column5: In this Charlotte Perkins Gilman work, the narrator is locked in her room at a guest-house to help her recover from post-partum depression, only for her to become manically obsessed with the title wall covering.
column6: The Yellow Wallpaper (do not accept or prompt on “Wallpaper”)

column5: This novel gets bonus points for having TWO languishing women: Mina Harker and Lucy Westenra. Abraham Van Helsing hangs garlic in their bedrooms when he realizes that the title vampire is draining their strength.
A multidimensional “landscape” named for this quantity plots genotype against it, and generally assumes that successful organisms fall into local minima. For ten points each,
Name this quantity that broadly translates to “evolutionary success,” since individuals with the greatest amount of it survive to reproduce.
column6: biological fitness (accept word forms like fittest)

column5: The concept of survival of the fittest drives this mechanism of evolution, which was postulated by Charles Darwin in The Origin of Species.

The notion that natural selection slowly explores rugged fitness landscapes, in which successful adaptations are very shallow local ditches, is challenged by this more radical theory of rapid-bursts of successful trait evolution, proposed by Stephen Jay Gould.
Frisky tourist agencies in this country warn of drop bears, which are predatory marsupials that will fall out of trees and attack visitors. For ten points each,
Name this country whose most dangerous animals tend to look more like taipan snakes or redback spiders, and less like koala bears.

By any reasonable set of criteria, the best Australian cryptid is this monster of Aboriginal myth that feasts on unsuspecting humans visiting billabongs. This animal is some sort of linear combination of bird, frog, and alligator.
Aboriginal creation myths speak of a “Rainbow” one of these creatures that inhabited the pre-historic Dreamtime and is associated with rainfall.
column6: serpent (accept snake; accept Rainbow Serpent or Rainbow Snake)

column5: These devices are often crystals of semiconducting material with a p-n junction. For ten points each,
Name these circuit elements that allow current to flow in just one direction.
For current to flow in one direction in a hypothetically ideal diode, this quantity for the circuit is zero in one direction and infinity in the other. This quantity is measured in ohms.

Light-emitting diodes can display different colors based on changes in the size of this region that separate occupied and empty energy levels. Semiconductors have small examples of this region, and doping can make them even smaller.
Give the following about spooky stories, for ten points each.
This Henry James novella is a ghost story about Miles, Flora, and the ghost of Peter Quint.
This author’s horror collection The Last Seance includes stories featuring Miss Marple and Hercule Poirot, who feature in her more commonly known genre of detective mysteries.

The cursed title object of this 1902 W.W. Jacobs short story “twisted [...] like a snake” after Mr White uses it to wish for two hundred pounds. In modern retellings, its fingers often curl to indicate that a wish has been made.
A 2022 wildfire damaged many of these sculptures in the Rano Raraku crater. For ten points each,
Name or describe these rock figures that were created by the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island.
column6: moai (accept descriptions of large stone heads; prompt on description of human sculptures, as some of the heads feature torsos)

column5: Large stone heads are a common motif in historical art. This Mesoamerican civilization, which invented a ball game popular in later cultures, carved large heads out of boulders in cities like La Venta.

Several Persian and Greek gods are depicted in massive stone heads on Mount Nemrut, which is in this modern-day country. A decidedly older ancient ruin in this country, C¸ atalhoy¨ uk¨ [chat-ull-HOY-ook], dates to nearly 10,000 years ago.
Give the following about 20th century philosophy Martin Heidegger, for ten points each.

Through works like 1927’s Being and Time, Heidegger was a major influence on this philosophical movement, later championed by Jean-Paul Sartre [sart] and Albert Camus [ca-moo], that studies how a human can “be.”

Beyond philosophy, Heidegger is best known for his membership in this German political party from 1933 to 1945. Heidegger later distanced himself from this party, but his posthumously-published notebooks include several examples of anti-semitism.
column6: Nazi Party (accept National Socialist German Workers’ Party; accept Nationalsozialistische Deutsche Arbeiterpartei; accept NSDAP)

column5: Heidegger’s less controversial post-war work includes The Question Concerning this concept, an essay that eventually defines it as including the “equipment, tools, and machines, the manufactured and used things themselves.” Stone tools and computers are commonly cited on opposite ends of humanity’s history of this concept.
Name some types of humanoid creatures with animal attributes from Greek myth, for ten points each.

One of these creatures, Chiron, taught both Jason and Achilles. Chiron was unusual among these creatures because his front pair of feet were often depicted as human, and only his back two feet were horse hoofs.
Naiads and dryads were two types of these feminine nature spirits. Echo was one of these creatures.
In art, nymphs have often been depicted frolicking with these masculine nature spirits that had the ears and legs of goats, similar to the god Pan.
column6: satyr (accept satyros; accept faun; accept silenos)

column5: Former Prime Minister of Pakistan Benazir Bhutto became the victim of this crime in December 2007, leaving her son, Bilawal Zardari, as her political successor. For ten points each,
Name this criminal-political action that was committed against Bhutto by someone using both a gun and a shrapnel bomb.
column6: assassination (accept word forms like assassinate; accept equivalents like murdering or killing a head of state)

column5: This politician was succeeded as Prime Minister by her son, Rajiv, after her assassination in 1984. This leader was assassinated by her bodyguards after her attack on the Golden Pavilion of Amritsar in her home country.
column6: Indira Gandhi (both underlined parts required; accept Indira Priyadarshini Gandhi with both underlined parts required; prompt on “Gandhi” alone)

column5: Gandhi’s bodyguards-turned-assassins were members of this religion. The Golden Temple is this religion’s central gurdwara.
column6: Sikh (accept Sikhi; accept believers in Sikhism)

column5: These chemicals are usually either lipids, such as testosterone, or proteins, such as insulin. For ten points each,
Name these chemical signals used throughout the endocrine system.
Most of the hormones produced by this gland found in the base of the brain, such as HGH and FSH, are proteins.

This peptide hormone is made in the hypothalamus but secreted by the posterior pituitary. This “love hormone” is responsible for the evolutionarily useful process of social bonding between parents and their newborns.
This novel’s protagonist romantically pursues Léon Dupuis and Rodolphe Boulanger [roh-DOLF boo-lawn-JAY] to distract from her boring life with Charles. For ten points each,
Name this novel by Gustave Flaubert [goo-STAHV floh-BAYR] about Emma, a frustrated woman who tries to become independent of her country doctor husband.
